claims.content: The VMU User maintains distributor records by capturing and managing master details of every distributor, including unique codes, names, addresses, business types, and contact information, to enable tracking of sales and distribution activities.

goal.raw_text: The VMU User maintains distributor records by capturing and managing master details of every distributor, including unique codes, names, addresses, business types, and contact information, to enable tracking of sales and distribution activities.

claims.content: VMU User
Master tables for geographical location details (District, Sub-District, County, etc.) must be established to support address data entry.
The VMU User accesses the Distributor Master Information screen to capture or manage distributor master details.

To add a new distributor record, the user selects the 'New' option and enters mandatory fields including Distributor Code, Name, Type of Business, Proprietor Name, and Address; optional fields include Designation, Contact No, Email Id, and Status.
The system validates that the Distributor Code is unique; if a duplicate name is entered, it issues a warning allowing the user to proceed with a differentiating indicator or change the name.
To update an existing distributor record, the user selects the 'Edit' option, modifies allowable fields, and saves changes.
To delete a distributor record, the user selects the 'Delete' option; deletion is permitted only if no child records (e.g., sales transactions) exist for that distributor.

The user may view the Sales History of a specific distributor by double-clicking on the distributor entry in the grid, which displays summary details such as Batch No, Date of Purchase, Qty Purchase, Qty Sold, Qty Returned, and Balance Qty.
The user may print the distributor master details or sales history report, subject to login permissions.

If a duplicate distributor name is entered, the system issues a warning message allowing the user to either proceed with the duplicate name (adding a differentiating indicator for reporting purposes) or change the name.

If the user attempts to delete a distributor record that has associated child records (e.g., sales transactions), the system prevents deletion; alternatively, the user may choose to deactivate or terminate the distributor using the Active/Deactivate option instead of deleting.
If the user attempts to save a distributor record without filling in mandatory fields (marked with *), the system prevents saving and likely prompts the user to complete the required information.
If the user attempts to print distributor master details or sales history reports without the necessary login permissions, the system denies the request.
The distributor master record is successfully saved with all mandatory fields (Distributor Code, Name, Type of Business, Proprietor Name, Address) and optional fields populated.
The system ensures the Distributor Code is unique; if a duplicate name is entered, a warning is issued allowing the user to proceed with a differentiating indicator or change the name.
Updated distributor records reflect the modified allowable fields upon saving.
A distributor record is deleted only if no child records (e.g., sales transactions) exist for that distributor.
If deletion is not permitted due to existing child records, the distributor can be deactivated or terminated using the Active/Deactivate option.
The system provides a provision to print the distributor master details.
Users can view the Sales History of a specific distributor, displaying summary details such as Batch No, Date of Purchase, Qty Purchase, Qty Sold, Qty Returned, and Balance Qty.
Other users have the provision to view the details of a distributor including purchase and sales details.
